result.rationale: The diff shows zoho-bigin's CalendarService.ts passing `credentialId` (the credential row's ID) to refreshOAuthTokens, while every other call site (google-calendar, hubspot, lark, office365, msteams, webex, zohocrm, zoomvideo) passes `credential.userId`. Since refreshOAuthTokens sends `calcomUserId: userId.toString()` to the sync endpoint, passing a credential ID instead of a user ID would resolve the wrong (or nonexistent) user's credentials. The mismatch is directly visible in the diff.

judged_text: This call site passes credentialId as refreshOAuthTokens' userId parameter (every other call site passes credential.userId), so the sync request sends calcomUserId=<credential row id>. The parent sync endpoint resolves that ID as a user, returning a different user's credentials or no credentials, so zoho-bigin tokens are synced for the wrong account or the refresh silently stores garbage.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new call `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument. The helper `refreshOAuthTokens` is defined as `(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId: number | null)` and, when syncing is enabled, sends `calcomUserId: userId.toString()` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. Every other updated call site passes `credential.userId` (e.g., Zoom, Webex, O365, ZohoCRM), so this one will send the credential row id instead of the Cal.com user id, causing the sync request to target the wrong user.
